channel.description: Latest articles from New York Daily News (nydailynews.com)

item.title: High turnover and red tape key obstacles as Mamdani admin outlines child care expansion plans
item.description: Mayor Mamdani ran on a campaign promise to dramatically expand free child care in the city to babies as young as 6 weeks.

item.title: Students at Queens school narrowly avoid being pepper-sprayed during accidental discharge
item.description: The pepper-spray was activated during a fight inside JHS 217 Robert A. Van Wyck Middle School located in Briarwood around 11:21 a.m., according to law enforcement.

item.title: FACT FOCUS: Misrepresented images spread after US and Israel strike Iran
item.description: Misrepresented images related to the war spread widely online.

item.title: Tennis stars in Dubai and Paralympians face travel issues as Middle East war continues
item.description: Numerous sports events in the region have shut down.

item.title: Nearly two-thirds of MTA subway work train locomotives out of service
item.description: Multiple sources confirmed that the locomotives are suffering from a maintenance backlog, with one source telling The News that, of those 115 engines, only 41 were able to go into service on Monday — 36% of the work-locomotive fleet.

item.title: Former Chancellor Aviles-Ramos takes gig at company doing millions in business with city schools
item.description: It's unclear if the new gig includes work on the company's dealing in New York, but city and state rules mostly restrict her from doing work within the five boroughs.

item.title: Daily Horoscope for March 03, 2026
item.description: Gentle waves move us toward needed changes. A Lunar Eclipse, also a Full Moon, in Virgo peaks at 6:37 am EST, nudging us to release habits and refine the systems we rely on. We can sort what stays, let go of what drains, and make promises we intend to keep with care, no matter how small. Later, as the emotional Moon opposes cerebral Mercury, feelings and words pull in different directions, so listening becomes the bridge. When we speak our minds, we can enact positive change.

item.title: Neck rash caused by ‘preventative skin treatment,’ Trump doc says
item.description: President Trump's doctor downplayed an unsightly red rash on the commander-in-chief's neck as the byproduct of a "preventative skin treatment."

item.title: Suspect in Texas mass shooting suspected of being terror attack had prior arrest in NYC
item.description: Diagne, a naturalized citizen and a native of Senegal, recently lived in the Bronx. A source also said he had one prior arrest on his New York record for illegal vending in Times Square.

item.title: Asking Eric: Husband thinks mother is perfect; wife thinks she’s a bully
item.description: Dear Eric: I have been with my husband for almost 35 years. We both had been married and divorced once. But there have been three of us in this marriage: my husband, myself and his mother. She has always treated me poorly and he always defends her. She has bullied me over and over again. […]
